summary: M.S. Computer Engineering (RIT, May 2026) with hands-on embedded systems and autonomous robotics experience. Designed and deployed real-time electrical control systems for multi-sensor robotic platforms, optimizing latency and reliability through bare-metal firmware and FreeRTOS task management. Proficient in system-level integration, from component selection and CAD to design documentation and end-to-end validation.

experience.title: Research Intern (Capstone)
bullets: Architected a full metal surface inspection pipeline combining custom image stitching, wavelet denoising, and depth estimation; validated on 3D crack profiles with ±8% error.
Optimized image-stitching algorithm through bit manipulation and wavelet bank design (alpha-blended sym6+bior3.5), improving PSNR from 65 to 86 through systematic signal processing.
Designed and deployed ZoeDepth monocular depth estimation for real-time surface reconstruction, achieving precise measurement accuracy under production-like inspection constraints.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Designed and fabricated a gesture-recognition wearable integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi, converting 3-DoF hand motion to HID commands via custom Python driver and Bluetooth (HC-05).
Implemented signal processing for z-axis differential thresholding with software calibration to resolve sensor jitter; achieved reliable tap detection over 200+ test cycles.
Produced full technical documentation and bill-of-materials for mixed-reality headset prototype using AI-based real-time chroma keying.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Led 25-member robotics team across national competitions, owning mechanical design, PCB fabrication, and AI/ML integration end-to-end.
Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE; implemented real-time sensor communication (UART, I2C) with closed-loop feedback control for locomotive robots.
Organized 10+ technical workshops and exhibitions covering Arduino, PCB design, and embedded firmware for 500+ students.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Architected a three-layer distributed system (Flutter client + Flask server + Jetson+Arduino controller) with unified WebSocket fabric; achieved 11.5s end-to-end voice-to-pick latency.

Integrated faster-whisper STT, Gemini intent classification, and TensorRT-optimized YOLO (5.2× speedup: 56.7→10.9 ms) for visual servoing; dual VL53L0X ToF sensors with TCA9548A I2C mux for contact-aware grasping.
Resolved 11 integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale frames); achieved 100% pick reliability over 10 trials through systematic debugging and component selection.
Implemented two-link IK on Arduino in C++; drove five servos with range-gated contact detection and interrupt-driven UART command processing.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built Cortex-M4 firmware in embedded C with timer-synchronized ADC scan conversions and interrupt-driven sample capture; deterministic 1 Hz update rate.
Implemented low-level I2C driver and GPIO/TIM2/ADC1 peripheral control in bare-metal C (no HAL); achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM footprint with predictable real-time behavior.
Programmed and verified in Proteus; demonstrated deep understanding of ARM Cortex-M4 timer/interrupt architecture and register-level peripheral configuration.

projects.name: Autonomous Driving in CARLA
bullets: Built automated data generation pipeline using CARLA's semantic segmentation; produced ~5,000 YOLO and ~3,000 UFLD training frames with zero manual annotation.
Trained YOLO11n (mAP50~0.85) and fine-tuned UFLD (ResNet-18) with custom loss functions; integrated into adaptive control stack with lane-following and waypoint fallback.
Validated in Town02 with 30 vehicles and 10 pedestrians; achieved zero collisions and correct traffic light compliance across multiple laps.
